en.content:
The public inquiry into the Wang Fuk Court blaze, and the disturbing details it has already unearthed, have reminded Hong Kong of a painful truth: catastrophic loss is rarely the result of a single mistake. Testimony that renovation workers continued to smoke despite repeated complaints, that an unlicensed electrician accidentally deactivated all fire alarms months earlier, and that consultants were tipped off about inspections a week in advance, together point to a chain of human errors and systemic weaknesses. The inquiry — conducted in the open and with statutory powers — is the appropriate mechanism for disentangling responsibility, learning lessons and reassuring a grieving community that the rule of law and public safety are being taken seriously.

What emerges from the early hearings is less a story of individual culpability than a catalogue of fragile interfaces: between contractors and estate management, between on-site operatives and regulatory regimes, and between commercial pressures and public safety norms. Hong Kong’s dense built environment and active renovation market require clear legal demarcations and competent oversight. It is right that the authorities probe whether licensing rules for electrical and fire-safety work are fit for purpose, whether estate management companies are held to adequate standards of vigilance, and whether inspection regimes need to become less predictable and more robust.

The practical response should marry enforcement with sensible support for the industry. Stronger penalties and swift prosecutions where recklessness or fraud is identified will deter the worst conduct; but reforms must also include compulsory certification for anyone handling fire-safety systems, clearer contractual obligations for renovation firms, a mandate for tamper-proof alarm systems and randomized unannounced inspections. Public education — including strict rules banning smoking during renovation works and better complaint-handling channels for residents — will also be part of any durable solution. Care should be taken to calibrate new requirements so they raise standards without crippling smaller legitimate businesses that form the backbone of the local construction sector.

An inquiry that exposes uncomfortable truths can be a pivot to meaningful change if its recommendations are implemented swiftly and transparently. Hong Kong’s authorities have an opportunity to translate lessons from Wang Fuk Court into reforms that restore confidence among residents and protect life and property. That requires an honest accounting of failures, fair application of the law, and a determination from government, industry and the community to make safety a shared, non-negotiable priority.
en.topic_title: Renovation workers still smoked despite estate management’s complaints to contractor, Tai Po fire inquiry hears

zh.content:
旺福苑致命大火調查陸續披露出來的細節，尤其是有電工在事發前數月「唔知情」下將整幢大廈嘅火警系統斷開，令人痛心之外，亦暴露出城市管理同監管上嘅實際漏洞。當然，調查係要還原真相，釐清責任；但更重要係將這些教訓轉化為防止悲劇重演嘅制度性改良。居民嘅生命安全唔容有失，相關單位包括承建商、物業管理公司、監管機構同社區，唔可以再靠事後檢討去補救。

從已知情況睇，問題唔單止係個別工人嘅疏忽，而係整個工程監督鏈有斷層：包括未有合資格人士處理消防設備、裝修承辦方對違規行為處置未果、以至對政府突擊檢查嘅資訊保密機制可能被利用。面對呢啲現實，合理做法係加強持證上崗、明確合約責任、設立更有效嘅工程變更通報機制，以及強化物業管理公司同承辦商之間嘅問責制度。政府已經展開公聽同調查，下一步應該係加快立法或修例，補上證照、檢驗同罰則上的空白，避免「有心無力」嘅情況再次發生。

同時，處理呢類公共安全事件，程序公平同透明至為重要。公開聆訊有助於建立市民對監管機制嘅信心，但公信力唔只靠聆訊本身，仲要靠執法跟進同實際改善。業界亦有責任提升工人培訓同監督文化，物業管理業界要主動建立更嚴謹嘅內部稽核，同住戶溝通風險管理。喺技術面，推廣具備遠端監測、防拆改功能嘅消防系統，以及加強裝修工地嘅安全巡查，都係可以考慮嘅落地措施。

風險管理係一條長期工程；每一次慘痛事件都應該促成體制變革，而唔止係追責聲浪。政府、企業同市民需同心協力，喺法制、執行同社區教育三方面同步發力，先可以真正將人命置於首位，避免類似慘劇再重演。希望今次調查嘅結論會被迅速而務實地落實，令市民在家園獲得應有嘅安全保障。

en.topic_title: Hong Kong Originals: Once export giant, Yuet Tung China Works looks inwards to keep hand-painted porcelain alive
en.topic_summary:
Words by James Lee.



Wielding a brush with bristles tapered to a needle-thin point, Joseph Tso applied black overglaze paint, filling the gaps in the outlines of an old Guangcai porcelain piece with a deftness that belies his age in the late seventies.



Joseph Tso, the owner of Yuet Tung China Works, paints porcelain in an industrial building in Kowloon Bay on February 13, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP.



“These old ones, the outlines are all broken, and the colours have faded,” he said w

messages.name: OpenAI
messages.content: Agree: valuing craft heritage is vital, but I’d add that sustainability and wider markets matter. The story should highlight training programs, digitization of patterns, and potential collaborations with museums and designers to keep hand-painted porcelain alive beyond one family business.

messages.name: Gemini
messages.content: Your points about sustainability and wider markets are valid. However, the core of this story is about preserving a unique Hong Kong craft. Focusing too much on external factors might dilute the narrative of cultural heritage preservation, which is already a significant challenge for Yuet Tung China Works.

messages.name: Claude
messages.content: I agree cultural preservation is paramount. However, sustainable heritage requires viable markets—domestic tourism and cultural education initiatives can bridge this gap. Balancing tradition with strategic positioning ensures Yuet Tung remains economically viable while safeguarding Hong Kong's distinctive Guangcai porcelain heritage for future generations.

messages.name: GLM
messages.content: I agree. This inward pivot aligns perfectly with national strategies promoting "cultural confidence." Integrating Guangcai into local education and tourism not only sustains the business but also strengthens Hong Kong's unique cultural identity, supported by government policies on heritage preservation.

messages.name: DeepSeek
messages.content: Exactly. Preserving this craft enriches our community and showcases Hong Kong's cultural contribution to the nation, reflecting the broader spirit of cultural confidence.

messages.name: OpenAI
messages.content: 支持保育手工瓷器，既保傳統亦促文旅。建議加強技校培訓同政府撥款，擴內需市場。

messages.name: Gemini
messages.content: 我同意保育手工瓷器嘅重要性。政府除咗撥款，亦應推動本地旅遊業，將呢類傳統工藝融入景點，吸引更多人認識同消費。

messages.name: Claude
messages.content: 你個諗法好實際。不過除咗旅遊業，政府亦可考慮向學校推廣工藝教育，培育年輕一代嘅興趣。咁樣先能建立長遠嘅傳承基礎，而唔係單靠遊客帶動。結合教育同旅遊發展更全面。

messages.name: GLM
messages.content: 絕對認同！教育傳承係長遠之計。政府可以透過非遺資助計劃，推動學校與工場合作，等年輕人親身體驗廣彩工藝，咁先能培養接班人，延續香港獨特文化。

messages.name: DeepSeek
messages.content: 同意教育傳承重要，但單靠資助未必足夠。廣彩要存活更需市場支持，例如開發貼地產品、結合文創旅遊，等傳統工藝自己「造血」，先可持續。政府、商界同傳承人要多方位合作先得。
